S1.Q2:
B's wall top is a flat L≈90 for rows 0–29 — constant at every x, no gradient — then rows 30–31 jump to L≈125 (a 2px lip catch), then rows 32–79 sit at L≈44 with L≈50 joint columns. That is a 46-point drop in two pixels, face at 0.49× the top, and the ratio is identical at x=8 and x=320. A has no such step: at x=232 the masonry runs 37→107 as a continuous run-time gradient down 85 rows, breaks to 65 at the y=85 line, climbs back to 89, then the floor starts at 101 — so the "top" plane's own internal gradient (70 points) is larger than its step to the "face" (42 points), and at x=40 that step is 42→28, only 14 points, and at x=400 it is 56→21. A's corner therefore exists only where the light happens to land; B's exists as material.
The second failure in A is what sits above the break: five stacked masonry courses at ~16px pitch with light mortar, receding into darkness to the top of frame. A top surface does not show five courses of face-brick. B shows one plane, 30px deep, with only cross-joints in it.
flips: Cut A's masonry field above y=85 from five stacked receding courses to a single top band ~28px deep, and turn its joints perpendicular to the run — short cross-joints every ~36px, matching the pin spacing — so the plane reads as stone tops rather than as elevation. Everything currently above that band stops being wall.

Author A's face-to-top relationship as a fixed material ratio instead of letting run-time light carry it: paint the face texture at ~0.5× the top texture's base value, and clamp the light's contribution on wall tiles so the top-lip-to-face step never falls below 35 luminance points anywhere in frame. At x=40 that step is currently 42→28; 14 points reads as fog, not as a corner.

Replace A's y=85 break — currently a flat 2px black line — with an actual lip: 1px light catch on the topmost row of the face, then 2–3px of hard shadow beneath it, so the crease has thickness rather than being an outline.

Give A's pins a third dimension: a 2–3px lighter cap across each pin's top edge, a 2px dark column down one consistent side, and a hard 4–6px cast shadow from each pin onto the wall face below and to one side. Nothing in A casts a shadow onto anything at present.

Break A's 256px pin clone: pins at 45/89/163/223 repeat verbatim at 301/345/419. Vary length by ±30%, lean two or three of them off vertical, and let the spacing follow where the wall actually failed rather than a constant cadence.

S2.Q1_WHY: A separates two planes by value — a flat top surface at 90 and a face at 47, roughly 2:1, with a 127 cap line on the seam between them; B's wall band and its floor are the same value once the run-time light is divided out.
S2.Q3_WHY: A's left wall (x0–13) is top-plane only at value 89 with no flank drawn, and the one object with two visible planes — the timber at x326–336, y40–53, orange top edge at y40–41 over a brown body — is clipped by the frame; B is elevation throughout, nothing in it terminates in a way that shows thickness.

S2.Q4_B: Dark 2px joints outlining every brick and an irregular rubble bond over two regular stretcher courses — nothing else; the one non-masonry element, a dark vertical strip at x200–207, y28–46 with two cream pixels at its base, is too small to read as anything, so effectively nothing holds it together.
S2.Q5_A: In use — bones scattered in loose clusters rather than laid out, drips running from joints where water would run — except the two pale grey debris shapes at x16–60,y58–80 and x285–292,y68–95, which are smooth-edged flat silhouettes with no stones in them and read as placed decals, not accumulation.
S2.Q5_B: Not posed, but not in use either — the same brick set tiled across the band and the floor's identical inscribed panel repeating on an exact grid make it read as a pattern rather than a place anything happened in.
S2.Q6_A: Generic — grey coursed masonry, brown dirt, skeletons is the stock version; only the replacement block and the timber suggest anywhere with its own rules. (Floor, out of scope: one dirt mottle cloned.)
S2.Q6_B: Generic — warm sandstone over rubble core reads as off-the-shelf tomb, and nothing in the wall states a rule. (Floor, out of scope: one panel tile cloned identically across the entire field.)
S2.Q2:
A's north wall is three tone-bands stacked in a fixed order down the screen: top plane y0–29 held at exactly 90 (91.5% of those pixels are literally 90) with 2px vertical joints at x=60,108,158,206,252,300; a 2px cap course at y30–31 at 124–147; then the face y32–79 at 44 body / 50 course-top / 37 mortar recess, on a 16px course pitch. The face at 47 mean is darker than the floor at 64, so the wall reads as under the light rather than in it, and rust drips hang *downward* from the joints at (150,73) and (175,72) — a cue that only works on a vertical surface.
B has none of this. Dividing out the torch falloff, B's upper rubble band (y4–48) reads 110, its brick courses (y74–104) read 117, its floor (y118–300) reads 113 — three planes within seven values of each other. The only mark at the presumed top/face seam is a black line at y50–53, and the brick coursing above it has the same pitch, proportion and orientation as below, so it is not a top surface — it is more face.
B's wall/floor junction at y≈107 is a single 2px black line with no lit lip above it, so the wall has no measurable thickness; the only reason it separates from the floor at all is that the torch happens to be low in frame.
flips: Split B's wall band into two albedo planes and hold them apart in the source art, before any run-time light: re-tone everything above the y≈52 seam as top surface at roughly twice the face's value, and keep only y≈74–107 as face. Target A's ratio — top ≈90, face ≈47 — not B's current 110 vs 117.

Add a cap: a 2px full-width band one to two steps brighter than the top plane, sitting on the near edge of the top where it meets the face, at B's y≈70–73. A's equivalent is y30–31 at 124–147 against a 90 top and a 47 face; B currently has a bare black line at y107 and no lip anywhere.

Re-lay the coursing on the new top plane so it is not the same bond as the face: A shows vertical joints only, at 48px pitch, with no horizontal courses on the top. B's rubble band currently repeats the face's horizontal coursing at identical pitch and brick proportion, which is what makes the seam read as a crack instead of an edge.

Separate the wall from the floor it stands on: B's floor field is 113 and its wall band is 110–117, so the silhouette exists only while the torch is close. Push the floor down or the top plane up to three distinct steps, as A does at 47 face / 64 floor / 90 top.
